explanation: King of Judah who reigned for 41 years and sought God's guidance in the beginning of his reign, but later relied on human help.
King of Israel whom Asa fought against and built fortifications at the border between their kingdoms.
King of Aram-Damascus whom Asa asked for help to defeat Baasha and his army.
A person who speaks on behalf of God and delivers God's message to the people. In this chapter, it refers to Hanani.
The prophet who confronted Asa with his mistakes and told him that he had acted wrongly by relying on Ben-Hadad instead of God.
A country in the Middle East that was home to King Ben-Hadad and his people.
God's strong displeasure and punishment resulting from human sin and disobedience.
Conflict between two or more parties, often involving violence and death. In this case, the war between Asa and Baasha.
An illness or weakening of health, here referred to as a disease in Asa's feet that led to his death.
